FN-525L3M6-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 176
Committee: Transportation, Utilities and Sponsor: Representative James Lomax
Infrastructure
Analyst: Jennifer Farish Date: 02/23/2024
House Bill 176 as introduced would increase the obligations of the Alabama Department of
Transportation (ALDOT) (1) in Fiscal Year 2025 by $600,000 to develop a statewide plan
regarding aviation technology infrastructure and $400,000 for a statewide education campaign
regarding aviation technology advancements; and (2) annually thereafter by an undetermined
amount dependent on the compensation of additional personnel hired pursuant to the
requirements of this bill. However, these obligations may be offset, in whole or in part, by
funding from ALDOT's Specific Service Signing Program (LOGO).

FN-525L3M6-2
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 176
Committee: Transportation, Utilities and Sponsor: Representative James Lomax
Infrastructure
Analyst: Jennifer Farish Date: 02/28/2024
House Bill 176 as reported by the Committee on Transportation, Utilities and Infrastructure
would increase the obligations of the Alabama Department of Transportation: (1) in Fiscal Year
2025 by $600,000 to develop a statewide plan regarding aviation technology infrastructure and
$400,000 to provide local and regional jurisdictions educational and technical resources to
support uniform planning and zoning language regarding aviation technology advancements;
and (2) by an undetermined amount annually thereafter dependent on any additional recurring
costs required pursuant to this bill.
This bill would also prohibit the Public Road and Bridge Fund, the Rebuild Alabama Fund, or
other state revenues used for federal match to be used for funding the statewide plan.

FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 176
Committee: Transportation and Energy Sponsor: Representative James Lomax
Analyst: Jennifer Farish Date: 03/14/2024
House Bill 176 as passed the House of Representatives would increase the obligations of the
Alabama Department of Transportation: (1) in Fiscal Year 2025 by $600,000 to develop a
statewide plan regarding aviation technology infrastructure and $400,000 to provide local and
regional jurisdictions educational and technical resources to support uniform planning and
zoning language regarding aviation technology advancements; and (2) by an undetermined
amount annually thereafter dependent on any additional recurring costs required pursuant to this
bill.
This bill would also prohibit the Public Road and Bridge Fund, the Rebuild Alabama Fund, or
other state revenues used for federal match to be used for funding the statewide plan.

FN-525L3M6-4
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 176
Committee: Transportation & Energy Sponsor: Representative James Lomax
Analyst: Jennifer Farish Date: 03/21/2024
House Bill 176 as reported by the Committee on Transportation and Energy would increase the
obligations of the Alabama Department of Transportation: (1) in Fiscal Year 2025 by $600,000
to develop a statewide plan regarding aviation technology infrastructure and $400,000 to
provide local and regional jurisdictions educational and technical resources to support uniform
planning and zoning language regarding aviation technology advancements; and (2) by an
undetermined amount annually thereafter dependent on any additional recurring costs required
pursuant to this bill.
This bill would also prohibit the Public Road and Bridge Fund, the Rebuild Alabama Fund, or
other state revenues used for federal match to be used to develop or update this statewide plan to
provide local or regional jurisdictions with educational or technical resources to support uniform
planning or zoning across the state.
